situational_uchi_soto.concept: The defining sociological organizing principle in Japanese pragmatics: In-Group (内 Uchi) vs Out-Group (外 Soto).

dynamics.with_outsiders: When speaking to someone outside one's company/family, all members of one's own company (including one's CEO or father) are treated as Uchi and referred to without honorific titles or Sonkeigo.
dynamics.internal: When speaking internally to one's CEO, the CEO is Soto/superior and receives Sonkeigo.

axes: Institutional rank (役職: 社長, 部長, 課長)
Customer vs Service Provider (お客様 / 店員)
social_rank_hierarchy.obligation: Linguistic choice of Keigo is not an optional stylistic polish, but an obligatory grammatical constraint.

discourse_aizuchi.definition: Frequent backchannel conversational listening responses indicating cognitive presence and attentiveness without interruption.

tokens.role: Formal acknowledgment of hearing the utterance.

implicitness_and_high_context.principle: High-context culture where explicit propositional assertion of negative refusal causes social friction (失礼).
implicitness_and_high_context.sasshi: Interlocutors are expected to infer implicit intent (察し) through subtle grammatical hedges (〜けど, 〜ですが, ちょっと...).
